candidates.title: [Bug]: range expression used as a value crashes the compiler (INTERNAL_ERROR: unexpected binary operator kind: ..<)
candidates.body:
### Description

A range expression that is not written directly as the collection of a `foreach` crashes BIR generation:

```
fatal[INTERNAL_ERROR]: unexpected binary operator kind: ..<
 --> range-value.bal:4:13
4 |     var r = 1 ..< 3;
ballerina: BIR generation failed
```
(With `...` the message says `kind: ...`.)

Spec §6.26 ([Range expression](https://ballerina.io/spec/lang/master/#range-expr)): "The result of a range-expr is a new object belonging to the object type `Iterable<int,()>` ..." and "a range-expr is designed to be used in a foreach statement, but it can be used elsewhere." So the program must compile and print `true`.

Related symptoms with the same root (the range value's static type is an iterator object with only `next()`, not `Iterable<int,()>`):
- `var r = 1 ..< 3; foreach int i in r { io:println(i); }` is rejected with `foreach collection must be subtype of object:Iterable` (expected output `1`, `2`).
- `object:Iterable r = 1 ... 3;` is rejected with `incompatible type: expected object&object { ... iterator() ... }, got object { public function next() returns nil|{| value: int |} }`.

### Steps to Reproduce

```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

public function main() {
    var r = 1 ..< 3;
    io:println(r is object:Iterable); // @output true
}
```
Run `go run ./cli/cmd run range-value.bal`.

### Affected Version(s)

`main` @ `00d6965be`

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions

Linux, built from source (`go run ./cli/cmd run <file.bal>`)

### Related area

Compilation

### Related issue(s) (optional)

#1302 (foreach over anonymous iterable object types) looks related to the foreach/type-checking symptoms, but not to the crash.

candidates.title: [Bug]: isolated class accepts non-private fields that are not isolated (only `public` fields are checked)
[Bug]: source text is not normalized: CR/CRLF kept inside string templates and a leading BOM is a syntax error
candidates.body:
### Description

Spec §3 ([Lexical structure](https://ballerina.io/spec/lang/master/#lexical_structure)): "After the sequence of octets is decoded from UTF-8, the following two transformations must be performed before it is parsed ...: if the sequence starts with a byte order mark (code point 0xFEFF), it must be removed; newlines are normalized as follows: the two character sequence 0xD 0xA is replaced by 0xA; a single 0xD character ... is replaced by 0xA". §6.6.1 says every character of a template outside an interpolation is a literal character, so the template's value reflects the normalized source.

Nutcracker does neither:
1. A string template spanning a CRLF line ending keeps the CR: `string \`a<CR><LF>b\`` has length 4 and bytes `[97,13,10,98]` (expected 3 / `[97,10,98]`). A lone CR inside a template also stays 13 (`[97,13,98]`, expected `[97,10,98]`).
2. A file that starts with a UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF) fails with `SYNTAX_ERROR: invalid token` at 1:4 instead of compiling.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. CRLF in a template. Create the file with CRLF line endings:
```sh
printf 'import ballerina/io;\r\n\r\npublic function main() {\r\n    string s = string `a\r\nb`;\r\n    io:println(s.length()); // @output 3\r\n    io:println(s.toBytes()); // @output [97,10,98]\r\n}\r\n' > template-crlf-v.bal
go run ./cli/cmd run template-crlf-v.bal
```
Actual: `4` and `[97,13,10,98]`.

2. Leading BOM:
```sh
printf '\xef\xbb\xbfimport ballerina/io;\n\npublic function main() {\n    io:println("ok"); // @output ok\n}\n' > bom-v.bal
go run ./cli/cmd run bom-v.bal
```
Actual: `error[SYNTAX_ERROR]: invalid token --> bom-v.bal:1:4`.

### Affected Version(s)

`main` @ `00d6965be`

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions

Linux, built from source (`go run ./cli/cmd run <file.bal>`)

### Related area

Parser

### Related issue(s) (optional)

None found.

candidates.title: [Bug]: relational and `==`/`!=` expressions on singleton operands are not singleton-typed
candidates.body:
### Description

When every operand has a singleton type (constants, literals), the result of `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `==` and `!=` is typed as plain `boolean` instead of the singleton computed at compile time. So `true ordered = MIN < MAX;` is rejected with `incompatible type: expected true, got boolean`, and a conditional expression with such a condition gets a union type (`expected string, got 0|"ordered"`).

Spec:
- §6.2.4 (singleton typing): "when all subexpressions of the compound expression have a singleton type, then the static type of E is a singleton subtype of T. This subtype is computed by evaluating the expression at compile-time".
- §6.27 ([relational expression](https://ballerina.io/spec/lang/master/#relational-expr)): "The static type of the result is boolean, modified by the usual singleton typing rules."
- §6.29 ([equality expression](https://ballerina.io/spec/lang/master/#equality-expr)): "in the case of the == and != operators, the static type is modified by the usual singleton typing rules; in the case of the === and !== operators, the static type is not so modified."
- §6.32 (conditional expression): if the static type of the condition is singleton true, the result type is the static type of the true branch.

Nutcracker already does this for `+`, `!` and `&&` (`3 t = 1 + 2;` and `false d = !true;` compile), and `const C = 2 > 1;` works; only relational and `==`/`!=` result types are left as `boolean`. Plain literal forms fail too: `true a = 1 < 2;`, `true b = "a" == "a";`. `===`/`!==` correctly stay `boolean`.

Expected: compiles and prints `true`, `true`, `false`, `ordered`. Actual: four `incompatible type` errors (lines 7, 10, 13, 16).

### Steps to Reproduce

```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

const int MIN = 1;
const int MAX = 10;

public function main() {
    true ordered = MIN < MAX;
    io:println(ordered); // @output true

    true same = MIN == 1;
    io:println(same); // @output true

    false lt = 2.0 < 1.0;
    io:println(lt); // @output false

    string label = MIN <= MAX ? "ordered" : 0;
    io:println(label); // @output ordered
}
```

### Affected Version(s)

`main` @ `00d6965be`

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions

Linux, built from source (`go run ./cli/cmd run <file.bal>`)

### Related area

Type checker

### Related issue(s) (optional)

#1262 (no singleton typing for `*`, `/`, `%`, shift and bitwise operators) and #1046 / #1096 (unary operators) are the same rule for other operators.
